proposals/window-tests.title: 2. Window tests: drive an interface in go test, with no display
proposals/window-tests.text: 2. Window tests: drive an interface in go test, with no display Status: in review · Author's approval: proposal ☑ (2026-10-21) plan ☑ (2026-10-21) Why Go UI's own tests already drive interfaces frame by frame: a private harness in ui_test.go makes an input.State of 800×600, moves a fake mouse, runs Begin , the interface and End , and reads where an element was laid out. Programs built on Go UI (an editor, a settings app, a game's menus) cannot use it: it is private, it uses a fake measurer of the test file, and it finds elements by hashing a label by hand. Each program ends up writing its own copy, or not testing its interface at all. Like Go's net/http/httptest , Go UI should ship a small public package for that: open a pretend window, press, type and wait in it, and ask what it shows. No display, no OpenGL, no cgo, so it runs in any go test and in CI. What The package is called uitest (chosen by the author: tests of a Go UI interface, as httptest tests a server). Its tests are written against an interface made only for them: a lighthouse keeper's log with a button, a check box, a text field and a dialog. Id Requirement Check R1 uitest.New makes a test window of a size in layout pixels, with a scale, a theme and a text measurer to choose (a measurer with fixed widths by default, so results are the same on every machine), and runs an interface function for one frame ( Frame ) or several ( Frames(count) ) exactly as a backend does: Begin , the function, End , the end of the input step test TestAFrameRunsTheInterfaceOnceLikeABackend R2 The pointer: move to a point or to an element, press, release, click, double click, drag from one point or element to another over several frames, and scroll tests TestAClickOnAButtonPressesIt , TestADragMovesASlider , TestScrollingShowsWhatWasBelow R3 The keyboard: press, hold and release a key, Tab and Shift+Tab, and type a text, one character per call or all in one frame tests TestTypedTextReachesTheFocusedField , TestTabMovesTheFocusToTheNextControl R4 Touch: put a finger down, move it and lift it, a tap and a long press tests TestATapPressesAButton , TestALongPressOpensTheMenu R5 Time: the window has its own clock, which only moves when a test says so ( Wait(duration) ), so double clicks, long presses and animations give the same result on every run test TestALongPressNeedsItsTime R6 Finding what was drawn: an element by its label or name (the one a screen reader gets, so labels that repeat are told apart by their scope), its rectangle, whether it is visible (on screen, not hidden by a scroll area or a layer above), whether it has the focus, and every text drawn in the frame in order tests TestAnElementIsFoundByItsLabel , TestAnElementScrolledAwayIsNotVisible , TestTheTextsOfAFrameComeInDrawingOrder R7 Failures come back as errors with a code ( uitest.element-not-found , uitest.element-not-visible , uitest.element-ambiguous , …), declared once in the package's errors.go ; nothing in the package panics or calls t.Fatal for the test. The message says what was asked and lists the labels that were on screen test TestEachErrorCarriesItsCode ; a test that a missing label gives element-not-found R8 The draw list of the last frame can be read as it is ( DrawList ) for tests that check colours or shapes test TestTheDrawListOfTheLastFrameCanBeRead R9 Go UI's own tests move to uitest where it does the same as today's private harness, so the package is used every day and stays honest go test ./... passes; the private harness is replaced wherever uitest does the same (the author's decision) R10 An example test that runs ( ExampleWindow , checked by go test ) and a guide page in docs/4-guides/ for someone testing their own program: open a window, click, type, find, and read an error the example's output is checked; the author reads the guide R11 Using the package costs nothing to programs that don't: it lives in its own package, the ui package does not import it, and no field of ui.Context is added only for it go list -deps of ui does not name uitest R12 Added by the author, 2026-10-21. A mode that shows the results in a Go UI window, visual and pretty: go run ./cmd/uitest ./... runs the tests with recording on and opens a window listing every test that used uitest , passed or failed, with its error codes and messages; for each test a replay of its frames, drawn from the recorded draw lists, stepped frame by frame, with the pointer, the clicks and the element each action found highlighted. Built with Go UI's own controls and theme (cards, icons, chips, the theme's colours), nothing hand-made where Go UI has a control. Recording happens only while the mode is on, so plain go test pays nothing tests with uitest of the viewer's logic (loading recordings, the list, stepping frames, the highlight); a test that a window with recording off keeps nothing; the window itself needs a display, so its look is the author's check R13 Added by the author, 2026-10-21. A control with no words of its own (an icon button) is read, by screen readers and by uitest , by the tooltip that follows it; with none, by its icon's name as before test TestAnIconButtonIsReadByTheTooltipAfterIt R14 Added by the author, 2026-10-21. uitest.ElementWithin(outer, inner) finds an element by its label inside another found by its label, with coded errors when either is missing or the inner one is repeated inside tests TestAnElementIsFoundWithinAnother , TestAnElementMissingWithinAnotherIsNotFound Out of scope A picture of a frame without a display: the viewer of R12 paints recorded draw lists in a real window, which needs a display. A PNG of a frame and golden images (the author's decision): Go Renderer has no software painter today (its software/ package is a stub), so there is no way to paint a frame without a display. Once Go Renderer can paint a draw list into an image.RGBA , a Picture method and a golden-file helper are a separate proposal. DrawList (R8) is what tests read until then. Testing through a real backend window ( window/ ): this package drives ui.Context and input.State directly; the backends keep their own tests. Recording a session by hand and playing it back. Game pads, and the screen-reader actions beyond what R6 reads (they already have ReaderPress and friends). Design The pieces uitest/ is a new package at the root, beside window/ . It imports ui , draw2d and input only; ui never imports it. Its files, one part each: File What it holds window.go Window : a *ui.Context , an *input.State , the interface function, the clock. New(build, options...) , Frame , Frames(count) , Resize , Context , State (an escape hatch for what the package does not cover yet) options.go Size(width, height) , Scale(factor) , Theme(theme) , Measurer(measurer) : functional options, so New(build) works with nothing else measurer.go FixedMeasurer : each character half the text size wide, as the private fakeMeasurer does today; the default clock.go the window's clock, set into input.State.Now ; Wait(duration) moves it and runs the frames that fall in that time at a fixed step ( frameDuration , one sixtieth of a second) pointer.go MoveTo , MoveToElement , Press , Release , Click , DoubleClick , Drag , Scroll keyboard.go PressKey , HoldKey , ReleaseKey , Tab , ShiftTab , Type touch.go TouchDown , TouchMove , TouchUp , Tap , LongPress find.go Element(label) and ElementIn(scope, label) return an Element (label, Rect , Visible , Focused , Pressable ); Texts() ; DrawList() errors.go the codes, at the top, and one constructor each example_test.go , *_test.go the tests named in What, beside the code Every action is one or more whole frames: an action changes the input state, runs Frame , and returns an error when its target is missing. Click is press, frame, release, frame, because a control in Go UI answers on release and needs the frame between. Finding elements The package reads the screen-reader tree ( ScreenReaderNodes ), which already gives each control its ID, label, rectangle (already clipped by scroll areas) and whether it can be pressed. The test window switches the screen reader on when it is made. Two small public additions to ui are needed, both generic and useful to any program: (*Context).FocusedID() ID : which control has the focus. Today it is private. AccessibleNode.Hidden , or an equivalent rule: a node under a modal layer is not visible. If the tree already leaves those nodes out, nothing is added; T2 checks which. Texts() walks the draw list for TextKind commands, so it also finds text that is not a control (a heading, a status line). Errors are a small type: Error{Code, Message} with Code a string constant, compared with errors.Is against a sentinel per code ( uitest.ErrorElementNotFound ), so returning one only allocates when a test fails. Codes: uitest.element-not-found , uitest.element-ambiguous , uitest.element-not-visible , uitest.element-not-pressable , uitest.invalid-size . Go UI's own tests Tests inside package ui cannot import uitest : uitest imports ui , and that would be a cycle. So the tests that only use public behaviour (click a button, type in a field, Tab through controls) move to package ui_test files and use uitest ; the tests that read private state ( ui.previous , the focus order, memory) keep a much smaller private harness. T6 lists which is which before moving anything. The results viewer (R12) Recording ( uitest/recording.go ): a window made with the Test(t) option and the environment variable UITEST_RECORD set to a folder keeps, for each frame, a copy of the draw list's commands, the pointer, the fingers, the action that ran it ( Click "Save" ) and the rectangle of the element that action found. Errors returned by the package are kept too. At the end of the test ( t.Cleanup ) it writes one JSON file per test into that folder, with the test's name and whether it failed. With the variable unset, Test(t) only remembers the name: no copy, no file. Pictures in a draw list are kept by size only (a grey box in the replay). The program ( cmd/uitest/ ): go run ./cmd/uitest ./... makes a fresh folder, runs go test with UITEST_RECORD set and the arguments given, then opens a window with the results. Its logic ( results.go : load the folder, sort failed tests first, step through frames) is apart from its look ( view.go ), so the logic is tested with uitest itself, headless. The look : a side list of tests as Selectable rows with a check or cross icon and a Chip for each error code; the chosen test in a card with its name, its messages and the replay: the recorded draw list painted with Paint , scaled to fit, the pointer as a ring, a press as a filled ring, and the found element outlined in the theme's FocusRing . Buttons and a Slider step through the frames. (The arrow keys were dropped while building: ui.Context gives a program no public way to read a key outside a scene.) Not taken : an HTML report (the author asked for a Go UI window); recording always (it would cost every go test ). Not taken Finding elements through a new private-state accessor on Context (a public map of laid-out rectangles): it would add a field read only by tests (against R11). The screen-reader tree is already public, already clipped, and already labelled. Methods that take *testing.T and fail the test themselves : shorter tests, but the author asked for errors with codes and no panics, and a returned error also works outside go test . Real time with time.Sleep : slow and flaky in CI. A PNG of a frame : no software painter yet (see Out of scope). Tasks [x] T1 — The window, its options, the fixed measurer and the clock: New , Frame , Frames , Wait · uitest/window.go , options.go , measurer.go , clock.go , errors.go · R1 R5 R11 · tests: TestAFrameRunsTheInterfaceOnceLikeABackend , TestWaitMovesTheClockAndRunsTheFramesInIt , TestEachErrorCarriesItsCode (for the codes so far), a go list -deps test that ui does not import uitest [x] T2 — Finding what was drawn: Element , ElementIn , Texts , DrawList ; FocusedID on ui.Context ; check that switching the screen reader on does not change the layout · uitest/find.go , ui/focus.go (no Hidden was needed: the tree already leaves out what is behind a dialog) · R6 R7 R8 · tests: TestAnElementIsFoundByItsLabel , TestAnElementScrolledAwayIsNotVisible , TestTheTextsOfAFrameComeInDrawingOrder , TestTheDrawListOfTheLastFrameCanBeRead , TestAMissingLabelGivesElementNotFound , TestTheScreenReaderTreeDoesNotChangeTheLayout [x] T3 — The pointer · uitest/pointer.go · R2 R7 · tests: TestAClickOnAButtonPressesIt , TestADragMovesASlider , TestScrollingShowsWhatWasBelow [x] T4 — The keyboard and typed text · uitest/keyboard.go · R3 · tests: TestTypedTextReachesTheFocusedField , TestTabMovesTheFocusToTheNextControl [x] T5 — Touch, with the clock for long presses · uitest/touch.go · R4 R5 · tests: TestATapPressesAButton , TestALongPressOpensTheMenu , TestALongPressNeedsItsTime [x] T6 — Go UI's own tests move to uitest where it does the same; the private harness keeps only what reads private state · *_test.go at the root · R9 · go vet ./... and go test ./... pass with the same number of tests or more. Moved: the three long-press tests of a finger and the two click tests ( longpress_uitest_test.go , controls_uitest_test.go ); the rest read private state ( ui.previous , ui.active , ids made with frameWithID ) or the right mouse button, and keep the private harness [x] T7 — The example and the guide: ExampleWindow (a lighthouse keeper's log: click a button, type a line, find it), docs/4-guides/11-testing-an-interface.md , a reference page docs/6-reference/3-uitest.md made by generate.py , links from the overview · uitest/example_test.go , docs/ · R10 · the example's // Output: is checked by go test ; the author reads the guide [x] T8 — Recording: the Test(t) option, frames and errors kept only while UITEST_RECORD is set, one JSON file per test · uitest/recording.go , options.go · R12 · tests: TestAWindowWithoutRecordingKeepsNothing , TestARecordedTestWritesItsFramesAndErrors [x] T9 — The results viewer: cmd/uitest runs the tests and shows them, logic apart from look; a guide section on it · cmd/uitest/main.go , results.go , replay.go , view.go , docs/4-guides/11-testing-an-interface.md · R12 · tests (with uitest ): TestFailedTestsComeFirst , TestSteppingStopsAtTheEnds , TestTheStepButtonsMoveThroughTheFrames , TestChoosingATestShowsItsErrors , TestTheFoundElementIsHighlighted , TestAFrameWithNoTargetHasNoHighlight ; the window's look is checked by the author on a display Result Built on feature/window-tests , one commit per task: Package uitest (R1–R8, R11): New with Size , Scale , Theme , Measurer , Test ; Frame , Frames , Wait ; the pointer, keys, typed text and touch; Element , ElementIn , Texts , DrawList ; errors with seven codes in uitest/errors.go . One public addition to ui : Context.FocusedID . AccessibleNode.Hidden was not needed: the screen-reader tree already leaves out what is behind a dialog, and a text covered by a higher layer is found not visible. Go UI's own tests (R9): five tests moved to uitest ; the rest keep the private harness because they read private state. ExampleWindow and the guide docs/4-guides/11-testing-an-interface.md , with its reference page (R10). Recording and the viewer cmd/uitest (R12). Checks run : gofmt -l . prints nothing; go vet ./... and go test ./... pass; every test named in What exists and passes; go list -deps of ui has no uitest . The viewer was run once under Xvfb with Mesa ( -capture ) on two made-up tests: it drew the list, the error card and the replay. Not built, or different from the plan : The arrow keys in the viewer: ui.Context has no public way to read a key outside a scene. A plain line of text (not a control) is found from the draw list, because the screen reader joins the texts of one box into one node; such an element is never Focused or Pressable . The not-found message lists the screen reader's labels, which may show joined texts. Test(t) reports a recording it could not save with t.Error : the one place the package fails a test itself, and only while recording is on. The replay (fixed after the first capture): the recording keeps each text's measured width and the theme's background; the viewer shrinks a line its fonts would paint wider, never enlarges the window, and draws the pointer only once it has been somewhere. Shadows are redrawn from their recorded size, only roughly. After each input the window runs one more frame and any frame asked for at once, as Go Renderer's on-demand loop does; found while trying uitest on go-engine's editor, whose workspace bar is drawn after the page it changes. For a person to review : all of it is AI-written and pending review. The viewer's look on a real display (light and dark), how it feels to step through a long test, and whether uitest is the API go-engine's editor wants, by writing one of its tests with it. Since (2026-10-21, asked by the author): the viewer lists every test go test ran, read from go test -json , by package: a test with no window shows its output; a window test keeps its errors and replay; play and pause step the replay.

reference/reference.title: Reference
reference/reference.text: Reference go-ui has four packages: Package Import What it is ui ui "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" The context, layout, every control, themes, screen readers window "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/window" A window that runs an interface: on the desktop, in a web page, on Android; preferences, notifications, films uitest "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/uitest" A pretend window for go test : press, type, wait and find what an interface shows, with no display uidrive "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/uidrive" Drive a real window by the names people see: find elements, play and record scripts, for demos, tutorials, replays and tests on a device ui.md and window.md list every type and function with the first sentence of its comment; they are generated from the doc comments ( python3 docs/6-reference/generate.py ). go doc github.com/akrck02/go-ui.Context.Table prints any of them whole. This page is the map: the context's methods by what they are for. The frame Method ui.New() (*Context, error) A context that measures text with go-renderer's fonts; NewWithMeasurer takes another (tests) Begin(state *input.State) , End() Open and close a frame: End lays out, paints and claims the mouse and keyboard. window.Run calls both for you Drawing() *draw2d.List What go-renderer paints: give it to scene.Overlay.Drawing once Push(name) , Pop() Open and close a scope, so controls in a loop have ids of their own Area(path...) (draw2d.Rectangle, bool) Where a control was drawn in the last frame, by its scopes and label RequestFrame(delay) Ask for another frame within a delay, for something that moves Size() (width, height) , Insets() The window's size, and how much of each edge the system's bars cover Theme (field) The tokens every control reads: ui.LightTheme() , ui.DarkTheme() Layout Method Box(layout, content) Arranges its children Frame(layout, look, content) Arranges and paints: fill, border, radius, shadow, clip Row(content) , Column(content) , Grid(columns, content) Shortcuts with the theme's gap Spacer() , Separator() Free space; a thin line ScrollArea(name, layout, content) Content that scrolls; ScrollOffset(name) , ScrollPull(name) Resizable(name, side, &size, minimum, maximum, layout, content) A box with an edge to drag Fold(name, open, duration, layout, content) A box that opens to its content's height and closes, with motion SwipeBox(name, layout, axis, content) A box a finger swipes sideways: pages, cards Sizes: ui.Fit() , ui.Grow() , ui.GrowBy(weight) , ui.Share(weight) , ui.Fixed(pixels) , ui.Percent(share) , each .Between(minimum, maximum) . Padding: ui.Pad(all) , ui.PadXY(horizontal, vertical) . Alignment: ui.Start , ui.Center , ui.End . Text and pictures Method Heading(text) , Label(text) , Caption(text) A title, body text, a quiet hint Text(text, ui.TextStyle{Size, Weight, Color}) Any size, weight and colour Icon(name) , IconSized(name, size, colour) A Lucide icon Image(picture, layout, radius) A draw2d.Image , cropped to fill its box Paint(layout, paint func(area, drawing)) A box you paint yourself, once laid out SetTextScale(scale) , TextScale() Every text larger or smaller (the system's font size) Controls Method Returns true when Button(label) , PrimaryButton(label) Clicked IconButton(icon, label) , PrimaryIconButton(icon, label) Clicked; square with an empty label FlatButton(label) , FlatIconButton(icon, label) Clicked; no fill until hovered (toolbars) Selectable(icon, label, selected) Clicked Clickable(name, layout, looks, content) Clicked: any box, with a look per state Checkbox(label, &value) , Toggle(label, &value) Changed Slider(name, &value, minimum, maximum) , SliderStep(…, step) Changed NumberField(name, &value, minimum, maximum, step, format) Changed TextField(name, &text) , TextFieldWith(name, &text, ui.TextFieldOptions{…}) Changed Select(name, &selected, options) Changed Tabs(name, &selected, labels...) Changed ListBox(name, layout, items, &selected) Changed Chip(icon, label, ui.ChipLook{…}) Clicked; RemovableChip returns clicked, removed MenuButton(icon, label, content) with MenuItem(icon, label, hint) MenuItem : chosen Tooltip(text) Explains the control before it LongPressed() The control before it was held, or right-clicked Text fields also have FieldFocused(name) , FocusField(name) , Focus(path...) , Typing() , the clipboard ( Copy(text) , ClipboardText() ), and for on-screen keyboards TypedField() and EditTypedField(edit) ; the bar over a selection is worded by SetEditingWords . Lists and tables Method List(name, layout, count, rowHeight, row func(index)) Equal rows, only those in sight built Table(name, layout, columns, rows func(*ui.Table)) A header and rows; table.Group(caption) , table.Row(key, selected, cells...) returns true when clicked Layers Method PanelWith(title, ui.PanelOptions{…}, content) , Panel(title, content) A floating card with a title bar, or docked to an edge Sheet(title, ui.SheetOptions{Width}, content) (dismissed bool) A modal card Modal(name, ui.LayerOptions{…}, content) (dismissed bool) Your content over everything, dimming the rest Overlay(name, ui.LayerOptions{…}, content) Your content over everything, without dimming Popover(name, &open, look, content) A box under the control before it Toast(text, warning) A short note at the bottom, fired once Pointer, touch and keyboard Method WantsMouse() , WantsKeyboard() Whether the interface claimed them in the last frame KeyboardNavigation ( WhenGiven , Always ), TakeKeyboard() , ReleaseKeyboard() , HasKeyboard() , FocusedID() When Tab, Enter and Space move between controls and press them, and when they stay with a game or a 3D view ( who has the keyboard ) LessMotion Held controls keep their size, for people who asked the system for less motion Pointer() (x, y) , Pressing() Where the pointer is; whether it is held Touches() The fingers on a touch screen Back() Answers the system's back (a phone's gesture); sheets and modals answer first DragSource(name, payload, layout, content) , DropTarget(name, layout, accepts, content) Drag a value of yours from a box to another Dragging() , DroppedOnScreen() A drag in progress; a drop on the open screen (the scene) Motion Method Animate(name, target, duration) float32 Eases a value to its target, asking for frames while it moves Appear(name, duration) float32 Eases from 0 to 1 the first time something is shown LayerOptions.Leave A modal or overlay leaves with motion Screen readers Method Describe(ui.Description{Role, Label, Value, Checked, …}) What the control before it is, for a screen reader SetScreenReader(on) , ScreenReaderOn() , ScreenReaderNodes() The list of what can be read, made each frame while one is on ScreenReaderAct(id, action) , ScreenReaderSetText(id, text) , SetScreenReaderFocus(id) What the screen reader asks, done in the next frame The window does all of this on Android; see the guide . The window Function window.Run(options, build) Opens the window and calls build every frame window.RunWith(context, options, build) The same with a context you made (to set a theme or a measurer first) window.Options{…} Title , Width , Height , MinWidth , MinHeight , Dark , Continuous , Backend , Canvas , Scene , MaxFramesPerSecond , Hidden , Shown , CapturePath ; RegisterFlags(flags) window.Wake() A frame, from another goroutine window.KeepPreference , Preference , ForgetPreference Settings kept between runs window.SystemPrefersDark() , SystemPalettes() The system's theme and, on Android 12+, the wallpaper's colours window.Notify , AskForNotifications , NotificationsAllowed Notifications on a phone window.OpenLink(link) , Share(title, text) , FeelLongPress() The system's browser, its share sheet, a buzz window.OpenVideo(film) A film the phone or the browser decodes window.Graphics() , LastCrash() What draws; the last crash's report, on a phone ← Documentation

reference/ui.title: go-ui
reference/ui.text: go-ui import "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" Package ui builds interfaces (panels, buttons, labels…) over a go-renderer view, in immediate mode: every frame the program describes the interface again from its own variables, and each control answers what happened to it (a button returns true on the frame it is clicked). Nothing has to be kept in step with the program's data, because the interface holds none of it. A frame goes: ui.Begin(state) // the frame's mouse and keyboard ui.Panel("Light", func() { // controls, nested in boxes if ui.Button("Switch on") { light.On = true } }) ui.End() // lay out, paint, claim the mouse if it is over the interface and world.Overlay.Drawing = ui.Drawing() makes go-renderer paint it over the scene. Layout is deferred: controls are boxes in a tree that is sized and placed in End, with rules like a flexible box (fit the content, grow into free space, fixed or a percentage, padding, gaps, alignment). Controls react to the mouse using where they were drawn in the previous frame, a frame earlier than they are drawn now: invisible at sixty frames a second, and it lets a box be sized by things declared after it. Constants and variables var EnglishEditingWords = EditingWords{Cut: "Cut", Copy: "Copy", Paste: "Paste", SelectAll: "Select all"} EnglishEditingWords are the bar's labels unless a program sets others (SetEditingWords). AccessibleNode AccessibleNode is one thing a screen reader can read and act on. type AccessibleNode struct { ID ID // the same from one frame to the next while the thing stays Parent ID // the scroll area it is in, or 0 for the window Area draw2d.Rectangle // where it shows, in layout pixels: the part a scroll area does not hide Description Pressable bool // a double tap presses it (ReaderPress) LongPressable bool // the program reads LongPressed after it (ReaderLongPress) Scrollable bool // ReaderForward and ReaderBackward scroll it, or move a slider Typing bool // the keyboard types in it now } Align Align places children inside the free space of their box, along one axis. type Align int const ( Start Align = iota // left or top Center // in the middle End // right or bottom ) Backdrop Backdrop draws a box's background in its area. type Backdrop interface { Paint(area draw2d.Rectangle, drawing *draw2d.List) } ChipLook ChipLook is a chip's own colours: its fill and the ink of its text and icon. The zero value uses the theme's quiet colours (Sunken and InkSoft). type ChipLook struct { Fill, Ink draw2d.Color } Column Column is one column of a table: its title, its width and where its cells sit. type Column struct { Title string // Width is the column's width. Use Fixed for narrow columns and Share for the rest: shares // start from nothing, so the header and every row come out the same. Width Sizing Align Align // Start for words, End for numbers // Weight is the face of its cells: draw2d.Mono for a column of codes. Weight draw2d.Weight } Context Context holds an interface between frames: what was where, what the mouse is on, which panel is in front, and the small state controls keep (a panel's position). Use one per window, from the goroutine that runs the update steps. type Context struct { Theme Theme // KeyboardNavigation says when the interface reads Tab, Enter and Space (focus.go). KeyboardNavigation KeyboardNavigation // LessMotion keeps controls still when the person asks the system for less motion: a held // control does not shrink. The program sets it from the platform's setting. LessMotion bool // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func New() (*Context, error) New returns an interface that measures text with go-renderer's default fonts, in the default theme. func from this name too. func (ui *Context) ReleaseKeyboard() ReleaseKeyboard gives the keyboard back to the program and takes the focus off the controls. func (ui *Context) RemovableChip(icon, label reference/uidrive.title: uidrive
reference/uidrive.text: uidrive import "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/uidrive" Package uidrive drives a Go UI interface by the names people see: it finds what the last frame showed ("Add an entry", "Light the lamp"), makes the input a person would give it, and plays a script of such steps frame by frame. A real window runs a driver through window.Options.Driver (a demo, a tutorial, a replay of a reported bug, a test on the device); uitest runs the same code in go test, with no display. Functions Function func KeyName(key input.Key) string KeyName is the name a script gives a key ("Enter", "A"), or "" for a key it has no name for. func Texts(context *ui.Context) []string Texts is every line of text the last frame drew, in drawing order: headings, labels, buttons' texts, a field's text. Constants and variables const ShownLayer = 1 << 20 ShownLayer is the layer a shown player draws on: above the interface's dialogs, popups and the screen reader's ring, so a demo's pointer is never hidden. var ( ErrorElementNotFound = &Error{Code: ElementNotFound} ErrorElementAmbiguous = &Error{Code: ElementAmbiguous} ErrorElementNotVisible = &Error{Code: ElementNotVisible} ErrorElementNotPressable = &Error{Code: ElementNotPressable} ErrorScriptNotRead = &Error{Code: ScriptNotRead} ErrorScriptStopped = &Error{Code: ScriptStopped} ) The errors to compare with errors.Is; comparing them allocates nothing. Action Action is what a step does, by the word a script writes for it. type Action string const ( MoveTo Action = "move-to" // move-to "Help": the pointer goes over an element Click Action = "click" // click "Save" DoubleClick Action = "double-click" // double-click "Entry" ClickAt Action = "click-at" // click-at 40 300: a place, for what has no name Tap Action = "tap" // tap "Light the lamp": a finger, as on a phone Hold Action = "hold" // hold "Lens" 1s: a long press, one second when no time is given Drag Action = "drag" // drag "Boat" 120 0, or drag "Boat" to "Harbour" Scroll Action = "scroll" // scroll "Log" -3: a negative amount goes down the page Type Action = "type" // type "Fog at dawn": the focused control takes the text Press Action = "press" // press Enter, press Shift+Tab Wait Action = "wait" // wait 0.5s Until Action = "until" // until "Saved" 10s: wait for an element, five seconds when no time is given ) The actions a script knows. Code Code is the stable name of an error: programs compare it, people search for it. type Code string const ( ElementNotFound Code = "uitest.element-not-found" ElementAmbiguous Code = "uitest.element-ambiguous" ElementNotVisible Code = "uitest.element-not-visible" ElementNotPressable Code = "uitest.element-not-pressable" ScriptNotRead Code = "uidrive.script-not-read" ScriptStopped Code = "uidrive.script-stopped" ) The codes this package returns. Function or method func CodeOf(err error) Code CodeOf is the code of an Error, or "" for any other error (and for nil). Driver Driver is what a window runs at each frame when it is driven. Drive comes after the window gathered the frame's real input and before the interface runs: it may add input to the state, and read what the last frame showed through the context. Show comes after the interface ran, and may draw over what it drew. type Driver interface { Drive(state *input.State, context *ui.Context) Show(drawing *draw2d.List) } Element Element is what the last frame showed of a control, a text or a scroll area. type Element struct { ID ui.ID // the one the interface gives it, 0 when it was not on screen Label string // what a screen reader calls it: a button's text, a described label Rect draw2d.Rectangle // where it was laid out, in layout pixels Visible bool // some of it shows: not scrolled away, not behind a dialog or sheet Focused bool // it has the focus (ui.Context.FocusedID) Pressable bool // a click or a tap does something to it } Function or method func Find(context *ui.Context, label string) (Element, error) Find finds what the last frame showed with this label: a button's text, a field's name, a line of text. func FindAt(context *ui.Context, x, y float32) (Element, bool) FindAt finds the smallest named element of the last frame under a place in the window, in layout pixels: what a person pressed there. func FindIn(context *ui.Context, path ...string) (Element, error) FindIn finds a control by its scopes (the names given to ui.Context.Push) and its label, outermost first: FindIn(context, "north", "Save"). func FindPressable(context *ui.Context, label string) (Element, error) FindPressable finds an element that shows and can be pressed: ElementNotPressable when a click on it would do nothing. func FindVisible(context *ui.Context, label string) (Element, error) FindVisible finds an element that shows, or says why it cannot be used: ElementNotVisible when it is scrolled away or behind a dialog. func FindWithin(context *ui.Context, outer, inner string) (Element, error) FindWithin finds an element by its label inside another found by its label: the button "Save" in the panel called "North". Error Error is an error with a code, and a message for people. type Error struct { Code Code Message string Cause error // what went wrong underneath, when something outside this package failed } Function or method func (err *Error) Error() string Error gives the code and the message. func (err *Error) Is(target error) bool Is tells whether target is an Error with the same code, so errors.Is compares codes, never messages. func (err *Error) Unwrap() error Unwrap is the cause underneath, for errors.Is and errors.As. Hand Hand makes the input a person gives with a mouse, fingers and a keyboard, on an input state, as a backend would: the first finger down also moves and presses the pointer, as a phone's backend does, so controls answer a tap as a click. It remembers what it holds, to let go of all of it. The zero Hand holds nothing. type Hand struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func (hand *Hand) Down() bool Down tells whether the main button, or the finger that is the pointer, is down. func (hand *Hand) HoldKey(state *input.State, key input.Key) HoldKey puts a key down; it stays down until ReleaseKey or LetGo. func (hand *Hand) LetGo(state *input.State) LetGo lifts every finger and lets go of the button and every key the hand holds: what a script does when it stops halfway, so nothing stays pressed. func (hand *Hand) MoveTo(state *input.State, x, y float32) MoveTo moves the pointer to a place in the window, in layout pixels. func (hand *Hand) Placed() bool Placed tells whether the hand has put the pointer somewhere in the window yet. func (hand *Hand) Press(state *input.State) Press holds the main button down where the pointer is. func (hand *Hand) Release(state *input.State) Release lets the main button go. func (hand *Hand) ReleaseKey(state *input.State, key input.Key) ReleaseKey lets a key go. func (hand *Hand) Scroll(state *input.State, amount float32) Scroll turns the wheel where the pointer is: a negative amount goes down the page, as a wheel turned toward the person does. func (hand *Hand) TouchDown(state *input.State, finger int64, x, y float32) TouchDown puts a finger on the screen. func (hand *Hand) TouchMove(state *input.State, finger int64, x, y float32) TouchMove moves a finger that is down. func (hand *Hand) TouchUp(state *input.State, finger int64) TouchUp lifts a finger. func (hand *Hand) Type(state *input.State, text string) Type types a text at once, as a paste or a fast typist does: the control with the focus takes it. PlayOptions PlayOptions choose how a Player plays. type PlayOptions struct { // Report, when set, gets a line for each step and one at the end (report.go): standard // output, Android's log, the 3DS's console. Report io.Writer // Show draws the pointer, the fingers and the element each step found over the interface, so // a demo or a tutorial is seen, not only run (show.go). Show bool } Player Player plays a script in a window, one frame at a time: it is a Driver. Each step finds its element in what the last frame showed, then gives its input over the frames that follow, as a person would, and lets one more frame show what it changed. A step that fails ends the script. type Player struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func Play(script Script, options PlayOptions) *Player Play makes a player for a script; give it to window.Options.Driver, or to uitest's Play. func (player *Player) Done() bool Done tells whether the script has ended: every step played, or one failed. func (player *Player) Drive(state *input.State, context *ui.Context) Drive plays a frame of the script. func (player *Player) Err() error Err is why the script ended early: the failed step's error, with its code. func (player *Player) Show(drawing *draw2d.List) Show draws, when the player's options ask for it, what it does over the interface: an outline around the element its steps found, the pointer as a ring (filled while pressed) and each finger as a dot. Recorder Recorder writes down what a person does in a window, as a script that plays it back: give it to window.Options.Driver, and take Script when the session ends. It adds no input. Steps name the elements pressed, so a replay works when the layout has moved; a press on nothing named is written as a click-at its place, and a drag that starts on nothing named is left out. type Recorder struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func Record() *Recorder Record makes a recorder. func (recorder *Recorder) Drive(state *input.State, context *ui.Context) Drive watches the input the person gave this frame, against what the last frame showed. func (recorder *Recorder) Script() Script Script is what the person has done so far, with the text they were typing. func (recorder *Recorder) Show(*draw2d.List) Show draws nothing: a recording is not seen. Script Script is a list of steps, played one after another. type Script []Step Function or method func Parse(text string) (Script, error) Parse reads a script: one step a line, blank lines and what follows a # left out. func (script Script) String() string String writes the script in the form Parse reads, one step a line. Step Step is one line of a script. type Step struct { Action Action Label string // the element the step acts on, by the name people see Target string // where a drag ends, when it ends on another element X, Y float32 // a click-at's place, or a drag's distance, in layout pixels Amount float32 // a scroll's turn of the wheel Text string // what a type step types Keys []input.Key // what a press step presses: the modifiers held, then the key Duration time.Duration // a wait's time, a hold's, or how long until waits at most Line int // the line it was read from, for errors; 0 when made in Go } Function or method func (step Step) String() string String writes a step as a script's line. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/uitest.title: uitest
reference/uitest.text: uitest import "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/uitest" Package uitest drives a Go UI interface in go test, with no display: it opens a pretend window, presses, types and waits in it, and tells what it shows. Every action runs whole frames, as a backend does, and returns an error with a code when what it looks for is not there. Constants and variables const ( InvalidSize Code = "uitest.invalid-size" ElementNotFound = uidrive.ElementNotFound ElementAmbiguous = uidrive.ElementAmbiguous ElementNotVisible = uidrive.ElementNotVisible ElementNotPressable = uidrive.ElementNotPressable RecordingNotSaved Code = "uitest.recording-not-saved" RecordingNotRead Code = "uitest.recording-not-read" ) The codes this package returns; the element codes are uidrive's, under the same names. const RecordVariable = "UITEST_RECORD" RecordVariable is the environment variable that turns recording on: a folder where each test made with the Test option writes what its window showed, for the results viewer (cmd/uitest). var ( ErrorInvalidSize = &Error{Code: InvalidSize} ErrorElementNotFound = uidrive.ErrorElementNotFound ErrorElementAmbiguous = uidrive.ErrorElementAmbiguous ErrorElementNotVisible = uidrive.ErrorElementNotVisible ErrorElementNotPressable = uidrive.ErrorElementNotPressable ErrorRecordingNotSaved = &Error{Code: RecordingNotSaved} ErrorRecordingNotRead = &Error{Code: RecordingNotRead} ) The errors to compare with errors.Is; comparing them allocates nothing. Code Code is the stable name of an error: programs compare it, people search for it. It is uidrive's, which finds elements for this package. type Code = uidrive.Code Function or method func CodeOf(err error) Code CodeOf is the code of an error of this package, or "" for any other error (and for nil). Element Element is what the last frame showed of a control, a text or a scroll area (uidrive.Element). type Element = uidrive.Element Error Error is an error with a code, and a message for people (uidrive.Error). type Error = uidrive.Error FixedMeasurer FixedMeasurer measures text with no fonts: every character is half the text size wide. Tests that use it give the same layout on every machine. It has every icon. type FixedMeasurer struct{} Function or method func (FixedMeasurer) HasIcon(string) bool HasIcon says every icon exists. func (FixedMeasurer) MeasureText(text string, size float32, _ draw2d.Weight, _ float32) draw2d.TextMetrics MeasureText gives each character half the size in width. Option Option chooses something about a test window; give them to New. type Option func(*settings) Function or method func Driver(driver uidrive.Driver) Option Driver gives the window a driver, which it runs at every frame as a real window does (window.Options.Driver): before the interface, to add input, and after it, to draw over it. func Measurer(measurer draw2d.Measurer) Option Measurer sets how text is measured; without it the window uses FixedMeasurer. func Scale(factor float32) Option Scale sets how many framebuffer pixels a layout pixel takes (2 on most phones). func Size(width, height float32) Option Size sets the window's size in layout pixels: what the interface's Size reports. func Test(test testing.TB) Option Test names the window after a test. func Theme(theme ui.Theme) Option Theme sets the interface's theme; without it the window uses ui's default. RecordedError RecordedError is an error a window returned, and the frame it came after. type RecordedError struct { Code Code Message string Frame int } RecordedFrame RecordedFrame is one frame: what was drawn, where the pointer and the fingers were, and the action that ran it with the element it found. type RecordedFrame struct { Action string // `Click "Save"`, empty for a frame run on its own Target draw2d.Rectangle HasTarget bool HasPointer bool // the pointer has been somewhere in the window PointerX float32 PointerY float32 Pressed bool // the main button or the first finger is down Touches []RecordedTouch // Commands are what was drawn; pictures are kept by their area only, and a text's Area.Width is // its width as the window's measurer measured it Commands []draw2d.Command } RecordedTouch RecordedTouch is a finger on the screen. type RecordedTouch struct{ X, Y float32 } Recording Recording is what a test's window showed, frame by frame, and the errors it returned. type Recording struct { Test string // the test's name, as go test gives it Failed bool Width, Height float32 // the window, in layout pixels Background draw2d.Color // the theme's, which a window paints behind the interface Errors []RecordedError Frames []RecordedFrame } Function or method func LoadRecordings(folder string) ([]Recording, error) LoadRecordings reads every recording in a folder, sorted by test name. Window Window is a pretend window that runs an interface function frame by frame. type Window struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func New(build func(context *ui.Context), options ...Option) (*Window, error) New makes a test window for an interface function: 800x600 layout pixels at scale 1, ui's default theme and FixedMeasurer, unless options say otherwise. func (window *Window) Click(label string) error Click clicks the middle of an element that can be pressed. func (window *Window) ClickAt(x, y float32) ClickAt moves the pointer to a place, presses and releases there, each with its frames, as a control answers when the button is let go. func (window *Window) Context() *ui.Context Context is the interface's context, for what this package does not cover yet. func (window *Window) DoubleClick(label string) error DoubleClick clicks an element twice with no time between, which the input state counts as a double click. func (window *Window) Drag(fromX, fromY, toX, toY float32) Drag presses at one place, moves to another over several frames and lets go there. func (window *Window) DragElement(label string, distanceX, distanceY float32) error DragElement drags an element's middle by a distance in layout pixels. func (window *Window) DrawList() *draw2d.List DrawList is what the last frame drew, as go-renderer would paint it. func (window *Window) Element(label string) (Element, error) Element finds what the last frame showed with this label: a button's text, a field's name, a line of text. func (window *Window) ElementIn(path ...string) (Element, error) ElementIn finds a control by its scopes (the names given to ui.Context.Push) and its label, outermost first: ElementIn("north", "Save"). func (window *Window) ElementWithin(outer, inner string) (Element, error) ElementWithin finds an element by its label inside another found by its label: the button "Save" in the panel called "North". func (window *Window) Frame() Frame runs one frame as a backend does: the driver if there is one, Begin, the interface, End, then the end of the input step, which forgets this frame's presses and typed text. func (window *Window) Frames(count int) Frames runs a number of frames, with no time passing between them (see Wait). func (window *Window) HoldKey(key input.Key) HoldKey puts a key down and runs a frame; it stays down until ReleaseKey. func (window *Window) LongPress(label string) error LongPress holds a finger still on an element for a second, letting the time pass, then lifts it. func (window *Window) MoveTo(x, y float32) MoveTo moves the pointer to a place in the window and runs a frame. func (window *Window) MoveToElement(label string) error MoveToElement moves the pointer to the middle of an element (see Element) and runs a frame. func (window *Window) Now() time.Time Now is the window's time. func (window *Window) Play(script uidrive.Script) error Play plays a script in the window, as a driven window would (uidrive.Player), with a sixtieth of a second passing on the window's clock at each frame. func (window *Window) Press() Press holds the main button down where the pointer is and runs a frame. func (window *Window) PressKey(key input.Key) PressKey presses a key and lets it go: one frame with it down, one with it up. func (window *Window) Release() Release lets the main button go and runs a frame. func (window *Window) ReleaseKey(key input.Key) ReleaseKey lets a key go and runs a frame. func (window *Window) Resize(width, height float32) error Resize changes the window's size in layout pixels, keeping its scale; the next frame sees it. func (window *Window) Scroll(label string, amount float32) error Scroll puts the pointer over an element and turns the wheel: a negative amount goes down the page, as a wheel turned toward the person does. func (window *Window) ShiftTab() ShiftTab moves the focus to the control before, as Shift+Tab does. func (window *Window) State() *input.State State is the window's input state, for what this package does not cover yet. func (window *Window) Tab() Tab moves the focus to the next control, as the Tab key does. func (window *Window) Tap(label string) error Tap touches the middle of an element that can be pressed and lifts the finger at once. func (window *Window) Texts() []string Texts is every line of text the last frame drew, in drawing order: headings, labels, buttons' texts, a field's text. func (window *Window) TouchDown(finger int64, x, y float32) TouchDown puts a finger on the screen and runs a frame. func (window *Window) TouchMove(finger int64, x, y float32) TouchMove moves a finger that is down and runs a frame. func (window *Window) TouchUp(finger int64) TouchUp lifts a finger and runs a frame. func (window *Window) Type(text string) Type types a text in one frame, as a paste or a fast typist does: the control with the focus takes it. func (window *Window) TypeOneByOne(text string) TypeOneByOne types a text one character a frame, as a person types. func (window *Window) Wait(duration time.Duration) Wait lets time pass: it runs a frame about every sixtieth of a second until the duration has gone, so long presses, double-click intervals and animations see time move as on a screen. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/window.title: window
reference/window.text: window import "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/window" Package window runs an application that is only an interface: a window with no 3D scene, where go-ui draws everything on the theme's background, in one draw call. On the desktop it opens the window through go-renderer (so it needs cgo, and Metal or OpenGL 4.1); built for WebAssembly (GOOS=js) the window is a canvas in a web page, drawn through WebGL2; built for Android (with gomobile) it is the application's activity, drawn through OpenGL ES. The window draws only when something happens: input, a resize, a frame a control asks for (a caret's blink, a tooltip due) or Wake. In between the program sleeps and uses no processor, which a laptop's or a phone's battery needs from an application that is mostly still. Set Options.Continuous for one that animates all the time. window.Run(window.Options{Title: "Lighthouses", Width: 1280, Height: 800}, func(context *ui.Context) { context.Label("Hello") }) Functions Function func AskForNotifications() AskForNotifications asks the person to allow notifications; on the desktop there is nothing to ask. func Feel(Feeling) Feel gives a buzz on a phone; a desktop has nothing to buzz. func FeelLongPress() FeelLongPress gives the buzz of a long press on a phone; a desktop has nothing to buzz. func ForgetPreference(name string) error ForgetPreference lets go of the value kept under a name. func Graphics() string Graphics describes a phone's OpenGL ES and GPU; on the desktop it is "". func KeepPreference(name, value string) error KeepPreference keeps a value under a name, replacing the one there was. func LastCrash() string LastCrash returns the report of the last run's crash; on the desktop the terminal shows it, and this is always "". func NotificationsAllowed() bool NotificationsAllowed tells whether the program may show notifications: not yet on the desktop. func Notify(id int, title, text string) bool Notify shows a notification; on the desktop it does not yet, and returns false. func OpenLink(link string) bool OpenLink opens a link in the application that shows it (the browser for a web page), through the computer's own command for that. func Preference(name string) (string, bool) Preference is the value kept under a name, and whether there is one. func Quit() Quit ends the program's window once the frame being made ends, as closing it would: Run returns. func Run(options Options, build func(context *ui.Context)) error Run opens the window and calls build in every update step, between the interface's Begin and End, until the window is closed. func RunWith(context *ui.Context, options Options, build func(context *ui.Context)) error RunWith is Run with an interface context of your own (a custom theme or measurer). func Share(title, text string) bool Share offers a text to other applications; a desktop has no sheet for that, so it returns false (put the text on the clipboard instead). func SystemPrefersDark() bool SystemPrefersDark tells whether the system is set to a dark theme. func Wake() Wake makes the window draw a frame now: call it when the program's data changes on another goroutine (a file loaded, a message arrived), since the window otherwise sleeps until input. Constants and variables var ErrVideoUnsupported = errors.New("window: films do not play here yet") ErrVideoUnsupported is OpenVideo's answer where films do not play yet. var PaletteTones = [13]int{0, 10, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 1000} PaletteTones are the shades' numbers in Android's names, in the order of each palette: 0 is white, 500 the middle, 1000 black. Backend Backend is the graphics interface a window draws through. type Backend string const ( Automatic Backend = "" // Metal on macOS, falling back to OpenGL if it cannot start; OpenGL elsewhere Metal Backend = "metal" // only on macOS OpenGL Backend = "opengl" // OpenGL 4.1, on every desktop system ) Function or method func (backend *Backend) Set(text string) error Set reads a backend from a flag: automatic, metal or opengl. func (backend *Backend) String() string BelowView BelowView is a scene seen from a camera on the 3DS's bottom screen. type BelowView struct { World *scene.Scene Camera camera.Lens Area *draw2d.Rectangle // where a computer shows it, in window pixels; nil is nowhere // Over draws it over the scene behind it in its area, with no background of its own (a radar // floating in a corner of the view); otherwise its area shows its own sky. A console's second // screen is its own, and keeps its background. Over bool } Feeling Feeling is a kind of buzz a touch gives, as a phone's own applications give them (Feel). type Feeling int const ( // FeelingLongPress is the buzz of a touch that became a long press. FeelingLongPress Feeling = iota // FeelingTick is a light tick: something chosen, a switch flipped, a step on a dial. FeelingTick // FeelingConfirm says something went through. FeelingConfirm // FeelingReject says something went wrong or needs a look. FeelingReject ) Options Options configure the window. type Options struct { // KeepStart gives the 3DS's START button to the program (a pause) instead of ending it; the // HOME menu still ends it. Elsewhere it does nothing. KeepStart bool Title string Width, Height int // window size in window pixels; 0 = 1280 × 800 // MinWidth and MinHeight stop the window from being made smaller than the layout needs; 0 = no // limit. MinWidth, MinHeight int CapturePath string // draw one frame to this PNG (hidden window) and return, for documentation and tests NoVsync bool // draw as fast as possible instead of waiting for the display Dark bool // start with the dark theme // Continuous draws every frame, at the display's rate, instead of only when something // happens: for an interface that animates all the time. It uses far more battery. Continuous bool // Backend is what draws the window: Automatic (Metal on macOS, OpenGL elsewhere), Metal or // OpenGL. In a web page it is always WebGL2. Backend Backend // Canvas is the id of the page's canvas to draw in, in a web page; empty = the first canvas. // The window is the canvas: Width, Height and Title follow the page. Canvas string // Scene, when set, puts a 3D scene behind the interface. It is called at every step after the // interface, with the input the interface did not claim (so the program can turn its camera // without fighting a slider), and returns what to show this frame: nil for no scene. On the // desktop a window with a scene draws through OpenGL. What it asks of that input's pointer // (LockCursor) and screen (SetFullscreen, applied on a page at the next key or click) reaches // the window. Scene func(state *input.State, step float64) *SceneView // MaxFramesPerSecond caps how often the window draws, to spare a battery; 0 = 60 on a phone, // the display's own rate elsewhere (where vsync keeps it). MaxFramesPerSecond int // Hidden is called when the program leaves the screen: on a phone, another application comes // up or the phone locks, and the system may end the program after that without a word; in a // browser, the page is hidden; on the desktop, the window closes. Keep what must survive then // (KeepPreference). It runs on the goroutine that builds the interface, except in a browser. Hidden func() // Shown is called when the program comes back on the screen after Hidden: on a phone, back from // another application or the lock screen (and at its start); in a browser, when the page shows // again. It is the moment to play again what Hidden stopped, such as a sound. On the desktop, // where a hidden window has closed, it is not called. Shown func() // Fonts are what the interface's text is measured and drawn in, a font file for each weight; // the zero value is go-renderer's default, the Go fonts. Fonts overlay.Fonts // Driver, when set, drives the window: at every frame it adds input before the interface runs // and may draw over it after (uidrive.Player plays a script: a demo, a tutorial, a replay, a // test on the device; uidrive.Recorder writes down what a person does). A person's own input // still arrives, and stops a Player. Nil costs nothing. Driver uidrive.Driver } Function or method func (options *Options) RegisterFlags(flags *flag.FlagSet) RegisterFlags declares -width, -height, -capture, -no-vsync, -dark, -continuous and -backend. Palettes Palettes are the colours a phone made from its wallpaper (Android 12 and later, Material You): three accent palettes and two neutral ones, each in thirteen shades from white to black, as Android names them (system_accent1_0 … system_accent1_1000). A program that builds its colours from them matches the phone, as the system's own applications do. type Palettes struct { Accent1, Accent2, Accent3, Neutral1, Neutral2 [13]draw2d.Color } Function or method func SystemPalettes() (Palettes, bool) SystemPalettes returns the colours a phone made from its wallpaper; a desktop has none. SceneView SceneView is a 3D scene seen from a camera, drawn behind the interface. type SceneView struct { World *scene.Scene Camera camera.Lens // Drawing is the program's own drawing over the scene and under the interface: a game's life // bar, a sight. On the 3DS it is painted on the top screen, in each eye when in 3D. Keep the // list between frames (Reset it), so drawing it allocates nothing. Draw it on layer 0: a higher // layer (SetLayer) covers the interface's menus and tooltips as well. Drawing *draw2d.List // Below is a second scene for the 3DS's bottom screen, with the interface painted over it (a // map, a turning model); nil leaves the bottom screen to the interface alone. On a computer it // is drawn only where its Area says: beside the scene (a preview of the console), or in a // corner of a scene that fills the window (a radar), under the program's drawing. Below *BelowView // Area is where the scene is drawn on a computer, in window pixels; nil is the whole window. // Around it the window shows the theme's background (a preview of a console's screen). Area *draw2d.Rectangle } Video Video plays a film's pictures (not yet its sound) in a draw2d.Image the program draws, with ui.Context.Image or any piece that shows a picture. A program opens it once, calls Update in every frame it is shown, and plays, pauses or loops it. On Android the phone's own decoders read MP4 and WebM films (H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, AV1); in a browser, those the browser plays; on the desktop, films do not play yet (OpenVideo says so). type Video struct { Loop bool // start again at the end // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func OpenVideo(film []byte) (*Video, error) OpenVideo opens a film (the bytes of an MP4 or WebM file, often embedded in the program), paused at its start. func (video *Video) Close() Close lets go of the film's decoder. func (video *Video) Duration() time.Duration Duration is how long the film lasts; 0 until known. func (video *Video) Ended() bool Ended tells whether the film reached its end (and does not loop). func (video *Video) Pause() Pause stops the film where it is. func (video *Video) Picture() *draw2d.Image Picture is the film's current picture, to draw; nil until the film's size is known. func (video *Video) Play() Play plays the film from where it is; at its end, from its start. func (video *Video) Playing() bool Playing tells whether the film is playing. func (video *Video) Position() time.Duration Position is how far into the film it is. func (video *Video) Update(context *ui.Context) Update brings the picture to the film's position, and asks for the next frame while it plays. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

the-quest/controls-and-forms.title: Lesson 3: controls and forms
the-quest/controls-and-forms.text: Lesson 3: controls and forms In this lesson the list becomes something you choose from, and the content a form that edits the lighthouse chosen: its name, colour, range, period, whether it is lit and whether it has a foghorn. Mission Pieces Time A form that edits the lighthouse chosen Selectable , text and number fields, selects, sliders 15 min The idea Each control is a window onto one of your variables : the field shows light.name and, when you type, writes into it. The list, the heading and the status bar look through their own windows at the same variable, so they always agree. The form of North Point: a name field, a colour select, a range with − and +, a period slider, a switch and a checkbox Choosing from a list Selectable(icon, label, selected) is a row that shows whether it is chosen and returns true when clicked. In a loop, each row needs an id of its own: two lighthouses could share a name, so each row opens a scope with its index. // sideList lists the lighthouses that match the search; a click selects one. Its right edge can // be dragged to make it wider. func (program *register) sideList(context *ui.Context) { column := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(8), Gap: 2} context.Resizable("side", ui.RightSide, &program.sideWidth, 180, 400, column, func() { for index, light := range program.lighthouses { if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(light.name), strings.ToLower(program.search)) { continue } context.Push(fmt.Sprint(index)) // two lighthouses may share a name: give each row its own id icon := "lightbulb-off" if light.lit { icon = "lightbulb" } if context.Selectable(icon, light.name, index == program.selected) { program.selected = index } context.Pop() } }) } The search box goes in the toolbar, after the Spacer . A text field edits your string in place and returns true on the frames it changes; here the list simply reads program.search at the next frame: context.TextFieldWith("search", &program.search, ui.TextFieldOptions{Placeholder: "Search", Width: ui.Fixed(200)}) The search "ea" leaves East Cape alone in the list For thousands of rows, List(name, layout, count, rowHeight, row) builds only the rows in sight, and Table adds a header, columns and groups ( the guide ). The form Each control takes a pointer to the value it edits, and returns true when the person changed it. A small helper lines the labels up in a column of their own: // field is a row of the form: a label in a column of its own width, then the control. func field(context *ui.Context, label string, control func()) { context.Row(func() { context.Box(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Fixed(80)}, func() { context.Label(label) }) control() }) } // details is the form of the lighthouse selected. func (program *register) details(context *ui.Context) { area := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(24), Gap: 12} context.Box(area, func() { if program.selected < 0 { context.Caption("Choose a lighthouse on the left, or add one.") return } light := &program.lighthouses[program.selected] context.Row(func() { context.Heading(light.name) context.Spacer() favouriteButton(context, &light.favourite) // lesson 5 }) field(context, "Name", func() { context.TextFieldWith("name", &light.name, ui.TextFieldOptions{MaxLength: 40}) }) field(context, "Colour", func() { context.Select("colour", &light.colour, colours) }) field(context, "Range", func() { context.NumberField("range", &light.rangeNM, 1, 30, 0.5, "%.1f nm") }) field(context, "Period", func() { context.SliderStep("period", &light.period, 1, 20, 1) context.Caption(fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s", light.period)) }) context.Toggle("Lit", &light.lit) context.Checkbox("Foghorn", &light.foghorn) context.Spacer() context.Row(func() { context.Spacer() if context.Button("Remove") { program.removing = true // lesson 4 asks first } }) }) } Until lesson 5, leave out the favouriteButton line. Notice what is not there: no "on change" handler copies the name into the list. The field writes light.name , and the list, the heading and the status bar read it at the next frame. The controls you used Control Edits Feels like TextField(name, &text) , TextFieldWith(…, options) A string Selection, the clipboard, undo, Tab to the next field; Placeholder , MaxLength , Secret Select(name, &index, options) An int A field that opens its list over everything; arrows and Enter work NumberField(name, &value, minimum, maximum, step, format) A float32 − and +, drag sideways, or click and type Slider(name, &value, minimum, maximum) , SliderStep(…, step) A float32 Click to jump, drag, Shift for fine steps Toggle(label, &on) A bool A settings row with a switch Checkbox(label, &on) A bool A box to tick Tabs(name, &index, labels…) An int A segmented row; show the tab's content with an if ListBox(name, layout, items, &index) An int A scrolling list of selectable items The full list, with buttons, chips, images and tooltips, is in the reference . 📝 The keyboard and the 3D view. While a field has the keyboard, Go UI claims it, so a 3D view's shortcuts do not take the letters you type ( lesson 6 ). Checkpoint Click East Cape : the form shows its name, colour, range and period; rename it and the list changes as you type; ea in the search leaves it alone in the list. Achievement unlocked: Clerk What you learnt Selectable rows in a loop, each in a scope of its own ( Push , Pop ). Controls edit the value they point to and return true when it changed. Every part of the screen reads the same data at every frame, so nothing needs syncing. Bonus (optional) Show a warning under the range when it is above 25 nm, in the theme's warning colour. ← Lesson 2 · Lesson 4: menus, sheets and notes →

the-quest/controls-of-your-own.title: Lesson 5: controls of your own
the-quest/controls-of-your-own.text: Lesson 5: controls of your own Go UI's controls are built from the same pieces you can use. In this lesson you make a favourite star from a clickable box, tell screen readers what it is, paint a strip of your own, and give the register a theme colour of its own. Mission Pieces Time A favourite star, and a theme of your own Clickable , Describe , Paint , Theme 20 min The idea Go UI's own buttons are made of the same bricks you can use: a box that reacts to the pointer, with a look for each state. And the theme is a paint chart : change one swatch and every wall painted with it changes. The finished register in the dark theme, North Point a favourite, its light's character painted under the period A clickable box Clickable(name, layout, looks, content) is any box that reacts to the pointer: it is painted with one of three Look s (left alone, hovered, pressed) and returns true when clicked. Inside, put anything. Go UI's own buttons are made this way. // favouriteButton is a control of the program's own: a star, golden while the lighthouse is a // favourite. A click flips it. func favouriteButton(context *ui.Context, favourite *bool) { theme := context.Theme square := ui.Layout{Width: ui.Fixed(36), Height: ui.Fixed(36), AlignX: ui.Center, AlignY: ui.Center} looks := ui.Looks{ Hovered: ui.Look{Fill: theme.Sunken, Radius: 18}, Pressed: ui.Look{Fill: theme.Line, Radius: 18}, } colour := theme.InkQuiet if *favourite { colour = draw2d.MustHex("#e8a317") } if context.Clickable("favourite", square, looks, func() { context.IconSized("star", 20, colour) }) { *favourite = !*favourite } // a screen reader would only hear "star": say what it is and whether it is on context.Describe(ui.Description{Role: ui.SwitchRole, Label: "Favourite", Checked: *favourite}) } It goes in the heading row of the form, after a Spacer (lesson 3 already calls it). Screen readers A screen reader (TalkBack on Android) speaks what is on the screen for someone who cannot see it. Go UI works out what to say from the boxes: a button reads its text, a checkbox says whether it is ticked. A box of your own holds only an icon, which would be read as "star". Describe , right after the control, says what it really is: ui.Description field Says Role What kind of thing: ButtonRole , SwitchRole , CheckboxRole , SliderRole , FieldRole … Label Its name Value What it holds Checked , Selected , Disabled Its state Hidden Leave it out: a decoration It costs nothing while no screen reader is on. The guide explains how the screen is read. Painting your own shapes When no control draws what you need, Paint(layout, paint) adds a box that is laid out like any other and then handed to your function, with its final rectangle and Go Renderer's draw2d.List to draw into: rounded rectangles, shadows, text, icons, pictures. The register shows a light's character , a mark for every flash in twenty seconds: // flashes paints the light's character over twenty seconds: a mark for every flash. func flashes(context *ui.Context, period float32, colour draw2d.Color) { theme := context.Theme context.Paint(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Fixed(24)}, func(area draw2d.Rectangle, drawing *draw2d.List) { drawing.Rectangle(area, 4, theme.Sunken, draw2d.Transparent, 0) const seconds = 20 for second := float32(0); second < seconds; second += period { x := area.X + area.Width*second/seconds drawing.Rectangle(draw2d.Rectangle{X: x + 2, Y: area.Y + 4, Width: 6, Height: area.Height - 8}, 3, colour, draw2d.Transparent, 0) } }) } // lampColours are the colours a flash is painted in, by colours' order. var lampColours = []draw2d.Color{draw2d.MustHex("#f5f0d0"), draw2d.MustHex("#d64545"), draw2d.MustHex("#3f9b5b"), draw2d.MustHex("#e8a317")} field(context, "Character", func() { flashes(context, light.period, lampColours[light.colour]) }) Coordinates are layout pixels from the window's top-left corner, like everything in Go UI. Themes Every control reads its colours and sizes from context.Theme : surfaces, inks, lines, the primary colour, text sizes, the height of a control, gaps, padding and corner radii. ui.LightTheme() is the default and ui.DarkTheme() its dark twin ( -dark , or window.SystemPrefersDark() ). Change a token and every control follows: func (program *register) build(context *ui.Context) { context.Theme.Primary = draw2d.MustHex("#00796b") // a teal of the register's own context.Theme.PrimaryTint = context.Theme.Primary.WithAlpha(0.12) … The register in its own teal Token Used for Background , Surface , Sunken Behind everything; panels and bars; wells and hovered controls Ink , InkSoft , InkQuiet Body text; secondary text and icons; hints Line , ControlLine Separators; the borders of fields and buttons Primary , OnPrimary , PrimaryTint The main action, the text on it, a light wash of it Positive , Warning , Danger States TextSize , HeadingSize , ControlHeight , Gap , Padding , ControlRadius … Sizes, in layout pixels Moving things Controls of your own can move. context.Animate(name, target, duration) eases a value towards a target and asks for frames only while it moves; context.Appear(name, duration) eases from 0 to 1 the first time something is shown; context.Fold(name, open, duration, layout, content) opens a box to its content's height and closes it to nothing. Checkpoint A star beside the name turns gold when clicked; under the period, a strip shows a mark for every flash; everything primary is teal. Achievement unlocked: Craftsman What you learnt Clickable makes any box a control, with a look for each state. Describe tells screen readers what a control of your own is. Paint draws your own shapes in a laid-out box; the theme's tokens colour and size everything. Bonus (optional) Make the star grow a little while the pointer is over it, easing between the two sizes. The whole program main.go : // Command register is the go-ui tutorial's program: a register of lighthouses, with a list to // choose one, a form to edit it, a search, a menu to add one and a sheet that asks before removing. package main import ( "flag" "fmt" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/draw2d" "log" "strings" ui "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/window" ) // lighthouse is the program's own data: the interface shows it and changes it, and keeps none. type lighthouse struct { name string colour int // an index into colours rangeNM float32 // how far the light is seen, in nautical miles period float32 // seconds between flashes lit bool foghorn bool favourite bool } var colours = []string{"White", "Red", "Green", "Amber"} // register is everything the program remembers between frames. type register struct { lighthouses []lighthouse selected int // -1 = none search string sideWidth float32 removing bool // the sheet asking before a removal is open added int // how many were added, to name new ones } func main() { options := window.Options{Title: "Lighthouse register"} options.RegisterFlags(flag.CommandLine) flag.Parse() options.MinWidth, options.MinHeight = 640, 400 // the smallest the layout still works at program := &register{ lighthouses: []lighthouse{ {name: "North Point", rangeNM: 18, period: 5, lit: true}, {name: "East Cape", colour: 1, rangeNM: 12, period: 3, lit: true, foghorn: true}, {name: "Harbour Mole", colour: 2, rangeNM: 6, period: 2}, {name: "South Reef", colour: 3, rangeNM: 15, period: 10, lit: true}, }, sideWidth: 240, } if err := window.Run(options, program.build); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } } // build describes the whole interface, in every frame. func (program *register) build(context *ui.Context) { context.Theme.Primary = draw2d.MustHex("#00796b") // a teal of the register's own context.Theme.PrimaryTint = context.Theme.Primary.WithAlpha(0.12) context.Box(ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow()}, func() { program.toolbar(context) context.Box(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow()}, func() { program.sideList(context) program.details(context) }) program.statusBar(context) }) program.confirmRemoval(context) } // toolbar is the bar across the top: the title, a search box and a menu to add a lighthouse. func (program *register) toolbar(context *ui.Context) { theme := context.Theme bar := ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.PadXY(16, 8), Gap: 8, AlignY: ui.Center} context.Frame(bar, ui.Look{Fill: theme.Surface}, func() { context.Icon("lighthouse") context.Heading("Lighthouses") context.Spacer() context.TextFieldWith("search", &program.search, ui.TextFieldOptions{Placeholder: "Search", Width: ui.Fixed(200)}) context.MenuButton("plus", "Add", func() { if context.MenuItem("lighthouse", "Lighthouse", "") { program.add() } if context.MenuItem("copy", "Copy of the selected one", "") && program.selected >= 0 { program.lighthouses = append(program.lighthouses, program.lighthouses[program.selected]) program.selected = len(program.lighthouses) - 1 } }) }) context.Separator() } // sideList lists the lighthouses that match the search; a click selects one. Its right edge can // be dragged to make it wider. func (program *register) sideList(context *ui.Context) { column := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(8), Gap: 2} context.Resizable("side", ui.RightSide, &program.sideWidth, 180, 400, column, func() { for index, light := range program.lighthouses { if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(light.name), strings.ToLower(program.search)) { continue } context.Push(fmt.Sprint(index)) // two lighthouses may share a name: give each row its own id icon := "lightbulb-off" if light.lit { icon = "lightbulb" } if context.Selectable(icon, light.name, index == program.selected) { program.selected = index } context.Pop() } }) } // details is the form of the lighthouse selected. func (program *register) details(context *ui.Context) { area := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(24), Gap: 12} context.Box(area, func() { if program.selected < 0 { context.Caption("Choose a lighthouse on the left, or add one.") return } light := &program.lighthouses[program.selected] context.Row(func() { context.Heading(light.name) context.Spacer() favouriteButton(context, &light.favourite) }) field(context, "Name", func() { context.TextFieldWith("name", &light.name, ui.TextFieldOptions{MaxLength: 40}) }) field(context, "Colour", func() { context.Select("colour", &light.colour, colours) }) field(context, "Range", func() { context.NumberField("range", &light.rangeNM, 1, 30, 0.5, "%.1f nm") }) field(context, "Period", func() { context.SliderStep("period", &light.period, 1, 20, 1) context.Caption(fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s", light.period)) }) field(context, "Character", func() { flashes(context, light.period, lampColours[light.colour]) }) context.Toggle("Lit", &light.lit) context.Checkbox("Foghorn", &light.foghorn) context.Spacer() context.Row(func() { context.Spacer() if context.Button("Remove") { program.removing = true } }) }) } // field is a row of the form: a label in a column of its own width, then the control. func field(context *ui.Context, label string, control func()) { context.Row(func() { context.Box(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Fixed(80)}, func() { context.Label(label) }) control() }) } // statusBar sums the register up at the foot of the window. func (program *register) statusBar(context *ui.Context) { lit := 0 for _, light := range program.lighthouses { if light.lit { lit++ } } context.Separator() context.Frame(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.PadXY(16, 6)}, ui.Look{Fill: context.Theme.Surface}, func() { context.Caption(fmt.Sprintf("%d lighthouses, %d lit", len(program.lighthouses), lit)) }) } // confirmRemoval asks before a lighthouse is taken out of the register. func (program *register) confirmRemoval(context *ui.Context) { if !program.removing { return } name := program.lighthouses[program.selected].name dismissed := context.Sheet("Remove lighthouse", ui.SheetOptions{}, func() { context.Label(fmt.Sprintf("Take %s out of the register?", name)) context.Row(func() { context.Spacer() if context.Button("Keep it") { program.removing = false
